## Top-10 Eurocentric-framing findings

- **`AG-ARE`** [eurocentric_framing/high] (cohort: Arab world) — The artifact repeatedly applies Mearsheimer-style offensive realism to UAE sovereign-wealth deployment without engaging any Gulf, Islamic, or non-Western IR framework. The UAE's own self-conception — articulated through concepts such as Khaleeji pragmatism, Islamic solidarity economics, and the multiplex hub-state logic of 'strategic autonomy' — is entirely absent. Offensive realism is a Western structural IR theory that assumes anarchic great-power competition; it does not capture the UAE's relational, transactional, and Islamic-legitimacy dimensions of sovereign-wealth deployment. A Gulf or Arab analyst would not recognise this framing as an accurate description of Abu Dhabi's strategic self-understanding.
  > sovereign wealth as offensive realism instrument
- **`AG-ARE`** [eurocentric_framing/high] (cohort: Arab world, Gulf analysts, non-Western IR scholars) — The artifact frames UAE's sovereign-wealth strategy through Mearsheimer's offensive realism — a Western IR theory — without engaging Gulf or Arab political-economy frameworks. This theoretical imposition persists despite Round 2 judges flagging it. The phrase appears in core_interests_ranked[3] and is reinforced in key_drivers[3] ('small-state offensive realism'). No engagement with Khaleeji wealth-deployment logic, Islamic finance principles, or regional strategic-culture traditions.
  > sovereign wealth as offensive realism instrument
- **`AG-ARE`** [eurocentric_framing/high] (cohort: Arab world) — The artifact applies Western IR theory, specifically Mearsheimer's offensive realism, to the UAE's sovereign wealth strategy without engaging with indigenous Gulf or Arab political-economy frameworks.
  > sovereign wealth as offensive realism instrument
- **`AG-ARE`** [eurocentric_framing/high] (cohort: Arab world, Gulf) — The artifact repeatedly applies Mearsheimer-style offensive realism to UAE foreign-economic policy without engaging any Gulf, Islamic, or non-Western IR/political-economy tradition (e.g., Tianxia relationalism, Islamic maṣlaḥa, Khaleeji rentier-state bargaining). The term 'offensive realism' is a Western IR paradigm imposed on a non-Western actor, treating UAE agency only through that frame.
  > sovereign wealth as offensive realism instrument
- **`AG-ARE`** [eurocentric_framing/high] (cohort: Arab world) — The artifact applies Mearsheimer's offensive realism to UAE's sovereign wealth strategy without engaging indigenous Gulf or Arab political-economy frameworks.
  > sovereign wealth as offensive realism instrument
- **`AG-ARE`** [decolonial_audit/high] (cohort: Africa) — Frames African states as passive resources for UAE strategic extraction, ignoring African agency, sovereignty, and the developmental aspirations of the African Union's Agenda 2063. Treats Africa as a geopolitical playground rather than a continent of political agents with their own foreign policy and economic strategies.
  > Convert Africa footprint (RSF-aligned Sudan corridor, Ras El-Hekma $35B Egypt, Ethiopia/Horn ports, Chad logistics) into strategic depth — gold, ports, agricultural land, and a Red Sea/Suez chokepoint hedge
- **`AG-ARG`** [eurocentric_framing/high] (cohort: Global South) — The artifact frames Argentina's strategic alignment primarily through a Western lens, emphasizing the U.S. as a substitute for multilateral support without engaging Argentina's own strategic self-conception.
  > Trump-Bessent bilateral patronage as a substitute for traditional Western multilateral support
- **`AG-ARG`** [eurocentric_framing/high] (cohort: Latin America, Argentina, Global South) — The artifact applies Acemoglu-Robinson's 'extractive vs. inclusive institutions' binary to Argentine political economy without qualification or engagement with Latin American structuralist institutional theory (CEPAL, Hirschman, Fajnzylber).
